newsitem.title: EGYPT: Big investors get Amriyah Cement shares.
newsitem.headline: Big investors get Amriyah Cement shares.

text.p: The Egyptian state's Holding Company for Metallurgical Industries sold almost one million shares in Amriyah Cement through the Egyptian stock exchange on Sunday at prices ranging from 67.01 to 71.00 pounds.

The operation was the first stage in the sale of about 3.4 million shares which big investors applied for in a sealed-bid auction earlier this month, one of the agents said. The 3.4 million shares make up 17 percent of the company's equity.

"The holding company decided to sell the investors everything they asked for. I am just waiting for the broker to tell me how many of the shares he managed to sell," said Nadir Ezzeddin of National Bank of Egypt, which handled the auction.
The sale, part of the Egyptian government's privatisation programme, will dilute the state's stake in Amriyah Cement to less than 50 percent, moving it into the private sector.

Data from the Egyptian stock exchange showed that the holding company sold 968,000 shares on Sunday in 28 deals. The largest single transaction was for 200,000 shares at 68.00. The shares had closed last week at 68.25 pounds.
The holding company received 38 bids for the shares and in some cases investors put in more than one bid. The names of the biggest investors were not available.
The state had negotiated to sell a large stake to the French building materials company Lafarge but Egypt declined to sell on the grounds that Lafarge was the only competitor.
